findings.vulnerability: RSA key generation is vulnerable to Shor-style factoring on a cryptographically relevant quantum computer. Plan ML-KEM or hybrid transition.
findings.recommended_replacement: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) for encapsulation; pair with AES-256-GCM for data at rest.
findings.migration_patch: # Replace with ML-KEM keygen + KEM encapsulation per your stack (e.g. liboqs / oqs-provider).
findings.hybrid_option: Combine classical ECDH/X25519 with ML-KEM via hybrid TLS or custom HKDF over both shared secrets.
findings.test_suggestion: Round-trip encapsulation/decapsulation tests; performance benchmarks vs RSA.

findings.vulnerability: ECDSA signatures rely on discrete log hardness; broken by Shor on ECC groups.
findings.migration_patch: // Use circl ML-DSA module or org-approved PQC library; update verification paths.
findings.hybrid_option: Dual-sign with ECDSA + ML-DSA until verifiers support PQC.
findings.test_suggestion: Cross-service verification tests; measure signature size impact.

findings.vulnerability: Classical ECDHE handshake does not protect against harvest-now-decrypt-later once CRQC exists.
findings.recommended_replacement: TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768 (or equivalent hybrid) on supported stacks.
findings.migration_patch: tls.Config{ MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13, CurvePreferences: []tls.CurveID{ tls.X25519MLKEM768, tls.X25519 } }
findings.hybrid_option: Prefer hybrid PQ groups where clients support them; retain X25519 fallback.
findings.test_suggestion: Negotiation tests with openssl s_client / browser matrix.
